clouds.name: Milky Way
clouds.description: The Milky Way, our home galaxy: a barred spiral about 100,000 light-years across holding a few hundred billion stars. The Sun sits in the Orion Arm, some 26,000 light-years from the centre.

physicsObjects.name: Sol
physicsObjects.description: The Sun, a yellow main-sequence star about 4.6 billion years old. It holds 99.86% of the Solar System's mass and circles the galactic centre once every 230 million years.

physicsObjects.name: Mercury
physicsObjects.description: The smallest planet and the closest to the Sun. An airless, cratered world whose surface swings from -180 C at night to 430 C by day.

physicsObjects.name: Venus
physicsObjects.description: Earth's near twin in size, wrapped in a crushing carbon-dioxide atmosphere. Its runaway greenhouse makes it the hottest planet, at about 465 C.

physicsObjects.name: Earth
physicsObjects.description: Our home, and the only world known to host life. Oceans cover 71% of its surface, and its large Moon steadies its tilt.

physicsObjects.name: Mars
physicsObjects.description: The red planet: a cold desert with a thin carbon-dioxide atmosphere, the tallest volcano in the Solar System, Olympus Mons, and a canyon longer than a continent.

physicsObjects.name: Jupiter
physicsObjects.description: The largest planet, a gas giant more than twice as massive as all the others combined. Its Great Red Spot is a storm wider than Earth.

physicsObjects.name: Sagittarius A*
physicsObjects.description: The supermassive black hole at the heart of the Milky Way, about four million times the mass of the Sun. Its mass was measured from stars orbiting it at thousands of kilometres per second.

physicsObjects.name: Saturn
physicsObjects.description: A gas giant known for its bright rings of ice and rock. It is less dense than water and has more than a hundred known moons.

physicsObjects.name: Moon
physicsObjects.description: Earth's only natural satellite, a quarter of its width. It circles Earth every 27.3 days and always shows the same face.

physicsObjects.name: Atlas
physicsObjects.description: A tiny moon shaped like a flying saucer, orbiting just outside Saturn's A ring. Ring dust piling up round its equator gave it its ridge.

physicsObjects.name: Mimas
physicsObjects.description: A small icy moon of Saturn covered in craters. The largest, Herschel, is a third as wide as the moon itself.

physicsObjects.name: Titan
physicsObjects.description: Saturn's largest moon and the only moon with a thick atmosphere. Under its orange haze lie dunes, and seas of liquid methane.

physicsObjects.name: Hyperion
physicsObjects.description: A tumbling, potato-shaped moon of Saturn so porous it looks like a sponge. Its deep, dark-floored pits are found nowhere else.

physicsObjects.name: Iapetus
physicsObjects.description: Saturn's two-faced moon: one hemisphere is as dark as coal, the other as bright as snow. A mountain ridge runs along its equator.

physicsObjects.name: Uranus
physicsObjects.description: An ice giant that spins almost on its side.

physicsObjects.name: Neptune
physicsObjects.description: The outermost planet. Its position was predicted from disturbances in Uranus’s orbit before astronomers found it.

physicsObjects.name: Pluto
physicsObjects.description: The dwarf planet with the bright, heart-shaped region revealed by New Horizons.

physicsObjects.name: Ceres
physicsObjects.description: The largest object in the asteroid belt. Dawn found bright salt deposits in its Occator crater.

physicsObjects.name: Vesta
physicsObjects.description: A large asteroid with a crust, mantle, and core. Dawn orbited it before heading to Ceres.

physicsObjects.name: Eris
physicsObjects.description: More massive than Pluto. Its discovery helped prompt astronomers to settle on a formal definition of planet.

physicsObjects.name: Haumea
physicsObjects.description: A fast-spinning, elongated dwarf planet with a ring and two moons.

physicsObjects.name: Makemake
physicsObjects.description: A bright, methane-ice-rich world in the Kuiper Belt, with one known moon.

physicsObjects.name: Phobos
physicsObjects.description: The larger, closer Martian moon. It’s irregular and slowly spiraling inward.

physicsObjects.name: Deimos
physicsObjects.description: The smaller, farther Martian moon, also irregular.

physicsObjects.name: Io
physicsObjects.description: Jupiter’s moon Io is the most volcanically active world in the Solar System, heated by tidal flexing.

physicsObjects.name: Europa
physicsObjects.description: An icy moon of Jupiter with strong evidence for a salty ocean beneath its crust.

physicsObjects.name: Ganymede
physicsObjects.description: Jupiter’s largest moon and the largest in the Solar System. It generates its own magnetic field.

physicsObjects.name: Callisto
physicsObjects.description: An ancient, heavily cratered world and the outermost of Jupiter’s four large Galilean moons.

physicsObjects.name: Amalthea
physicsObjects.description: A small, reddish, irregular moon orbiting closer to Jupiter than Io.

physicsObjects.name: Himalia
physicsObjects.description: A distant, irregular moon of Jupiter that lends its name to a group of moons with similar orbits.

physicsObjects.name: Enceladus
physicsObjects.description: This icy moon of Saturn sprays water vapor and ice grains from a subsurface ocean into space.

physicsObjects.name: Tethys
physicsObjects.description: A moon of Saturn with a huge impact crater and a canyon system that stretches across much of the moon.

physicsObjects.name: Dione
physicsObjects.description: A moon of Saturn known for bright cliffs of exposed ice that look like wisps from afar.

physicsObjects.name: Rhea
physicsObjects.description: Saturn’s second-largest moon, an icy world with a heavily cratered surface.

physicsObjects.name: Phoebe
physicsObjects.description: A dark, distant moon probably captured by Saturn. Its debris feeds an enormous, faint ring.

physicsObjects.name: Pan
physicsObjects.description: The ravioli-shaped moon orbiting inside a gap in Saturn’s rings.

physicsObjects.name: Daphnis
physicsObjects.description: A moon of Saturn that makes waves along the edges of the ring gap it orbits in.

physicsObjects.name: Prometheus
physicsObjects.description: A moon of Saturn that pulls strands of material out of Saturn’s narrow F ring.

physicsObjects.name: Janus
physicsObjects.description: A moon of Saturn that shares nearly the same orbit with Epimetheus. They periodically swap which one orbits closer to Saturn.

physicsObjects.name: Epimetheus
physicsObjects.description: A moon of Saturn that periodically swaps orbital positions with Janus.

physicsObjects.name: Miranda
physicsObjects.description: A moon of Uranus that looks like a patchwork of cliffs, grooves, and older cratered terrain.

physicsObjects.name: Ariel
physicsObjects.description: A bright icy moon of Uranus crossed by deep valleys.

physicsObjects.name: Umbriel
physicsObjects.description: The darkest of Uranus’s five major moons, with a conspicuous bright ring inside a crater.

physicsObjects.name: Titania
physicsObjects.description: Uranus’s largest moon, with extensive fractures and canyons.

physicsObjects.name: Oberon
physicsObjects.description: The outermost of Uranus’s five major moons, with an old, heavily cratered surface.

physicsObjects.name: Proteus
physicsObjects.description: Neptune’s second-largest moon and visibly irregular despite being about 400 kilometers across.

physicsObjects.name: Triton
physicsObjects.description: A large, likely captured world that orbits backward around Neptune and has active plumes.

physicsObjects.name: Nereid
physicsObjects.description: A moon with an unusually elongated orbit that takes it far from Neptune and then much closer again.

physicsObjects.name: Charon
physicsObjects.description: So large relative to Pluto that their shared center of mass lies outside Pluto.

physicsObjects.name: Nix
physicsObjects.description: One of Pluto’s small, irregular moons imaged by New Horizons.

physicsObjects.name: Hydra
physicsObjects.description: The outermost of Pluto’s five moons, with a bright, water-ice-rich surface.
